## Shipdeck 0.9.3 for Windows and Linux

The first release of Shipdeck for Windows and Linux: the same control center as the Mac app (products, sessions with
Claude, the built-in browser, App Store Connect, Google Play, Delivery, the roadmap and release checklist, Marketing and
jobs), with the same data files, so a portfolio can move between the apps. Uploading builds to App Store Connect needs
Xcode, which runs only on a Mac; everything else in App Store Connect works here.

- **Websites at their desktop layout.** Pages in the browser sidebar show the layout they have on a laptop, drawn to
  fit, instead of their phone layout. For a site whose text gets too small, the button in the address bar fits that
  site to the sidebar, and Shipdeck remembers your choice.
- **Claude can test the site you're building.** On localhost and the sites you add in Settings › Browser, a session can
  sign in with the test accounts you keep there, read the console and network requests, and run scripts in the page.
  It never sees the passwords, which stay in Windows Credential Manager or your Linux keyring, and it asks you before
  signing in to a site for the first time.
- **Your Claude Command everywhere.** The Claude Command in Settings › General (an alias or PowerShell function for
  another Claude account, such as claude-work) now also runs adding a product, Sync with Code and background jobs, and
  the Claude Code line for connecting an AI tool uses it. Shipdeck checks Claude again a second after you change it.
- **Google Play, one game at a time.** A product with many games links each one on its own. Create… opens Play
  Console's Create app page with the name and package filled in, for a game that isn't on Google Play yet.
- **Claude works more reliably in the browser.** Tabs you aren't looking at keep loading, dialogs and downloads work,
  and two sessions no longer take over the same tab.
- **Reddit jobs.** Products with subreddits get two job templates: check your posts every evening, and draft replies to
  new comments.
- **App Store.** A build in Processing for over an hour shows up as needing attention (Apple sends no email for it),
  and the Reviews page shows star ratings in every country.
- **Fixes.** A new browser tab's address bar is ready for typing. Submitting to the App Store no longer asks for a
  category you already chose, and a rejected version can be submitted again.
